name: PulsePoint AerExpand Pulmonary Efficiency Implant
body_location: thoracic — subpleural mesh lining both lungs, diaphragmatic anchor nodes at costal margin
description:
AerExpand is a subpleural biocompatible mesh system that lines the inner surface of both lung lobes and anchors at the costal margin of the diaphragm via a series of flexible tension nodes. The mesh is composed of a gas-permeable polymer lattice that does not interfere with normal alveolar gas exchange but provides structural support that increases functional residual capacity — the volume of air the lungs can hold at rest — by an average of 18 to 22 percent. During high-demand respiratory effort, the diaphragmatic tension nodes assist the diaphragm's downward displacement, effectively deepening each breath with less muscular effort. A secondary function involves the embedded capillary-level oxygen sensors within the mesh that monitor blood oxygen saturation continuously and trigger a subtle increase in respiratory drive efficiency when saturation begins to drop, helping users maintain performance longer before hypoxic degradation sets in. The system requires no external power, operating entirely through passive biomechanical interaction and the body's own respiratory cycle.

AerExpand was initially marketed to competitive athletes and free divers, and those communities remain enthusiastic adopters, but the implant's real commercial success came from the performing arts and service industries. Singers — particularly those performing in large venues without electronic amplification, a growing aesthetic trend in Meridian 88 — use it to increase breath support for sustained phrasing and projection. Teachers who lecture for six hours a day, street vendors, tour guides, emergency dispatchers who spend shifts talking, and labor organizers who address crowds on the Shelf have all found that the improved respiratory efficiency reduces vocal fatigue and maintains cognitive sharpness through long demanding days. Underwater construction workers at the Lake Michigan infrastructure projects use it as a safety buffer during shallow dives.
installation_requirements: Requires a licensed pulmonary biotech specialist; installation is an outpatient surgical procedure lasting 3–4 hours under general anesthetic; one night observation recommended; not available at pharmacy kiosks
maintenance: Annual pulmonary function test to verify mesh integrity and anchor node tension; no firmware updates required for base model; mesh is biologically inert and does not degrade under normal conditions; full replacement estimated at 15–20 years

side_effects: mild chest tightness and a sensation of pressure for the first 3–4 weeks as the body adjusts to the subpleural mesh
occasional brief dry cough during the initial integration period
some users report an unusual awareness of their breathing — a heightened consciousness of respiratory rhythm — that fades over several months
rare cases of pleuritis at mesh edges, typically resolving with anti-inflammatory medication
cultural_context: Among the performing arts communities of Meridian 88's Tier 2 and 3 neighborhoods, AerExpand has become quietly aspirational — the implant serious vocalists save up for, the way a musician once saved for a quality instrument. There is no particular stigma attached to it; breath support has always been a technical craft element, and few audience members consider the implant's role any more than they consider a singer's years of training. In athletic communities, its use in competitive contexts is regulated by league-specific rules, with some amateur athletics governing bodies requiring disclosure while professional leagues have largely accepted it as standard equipment. On the Shelf, it is sometimes obtained through subsidized programs for workers in dust-heavy or chemically exposed environments where the extra respiratory reserve provides a meaningful safety margin.
known_users: professional and semi-professional singers and vocalists
competitive free divers and underwater construction workers
street vendors and market traders who project voice all day
emergency dispatchers and crisis line operators
story_hooks: A celebrated singer in Meridian 88's Tier 3 music scene collapses mid-performance; medical examination reveals her AerExpand mesh has partially detached from a diaphragmatic anchor node — and the batch number traces to a recall that was quietly suppressed by a PulsePoint regional distributor to avoid the cost of a public notice.

An amateur athletics governing body has hired investigators to identify competitors who are using undisclosed AerExpand implants in a breath-hold diving competition where the implant is prohibited — the players are either the investigators, the competitors, or the people who installed the implants off the books.

A labor organizer famous for her ability to address crowds for hours without losing her voice is found dead, and her AerExpand implant's sensor log — if the players can extract it — contains a continuous record of her final hours, including the voices of everyone in the room when she died.
